questions.question_prompt: Why does burning fossil petrol contribute to climate change?
questions.keyed_answer: It adds carbon dioxide from long-stored carbon to the atmosphere.
questions.teaching_excerpt: emissions 3 Contents Understand emissions Emissions explained · Fossil carbon and a cold catalyst. Fossil petrol contains carbon stored for millions of years. Burning it combines that carbon with oxygen and releases CO₂ into the atmosphere. The added CO₂ strengthens the natural greenhouse effect and contributes to warming. Long-stored carbon: Naturvårdsverket · Climate effect: Trafikverket A conventional petrol car's three-way catalyst reduces carbon monoxide, hydrocarbons and nitrogen oxides by chemical conversion. It needs sufficient heat to become effective, so it is least effective just after a cold start. Conversion products include water and CO₂: cleaning up these pollutants does not capture the fossil carbon or cancel its climate impact. No single warm-up time applies to every car. Transportstyrelsen: catalyst operation, page 24 · Trafikverket: cold emission controls Pollutant comparison. Keep CO distinct from CO₂. The table summarises different mechanisms; one cleaner exhaust measure cannot stand for all of them. Substance Why it matters CO₂ · carbon dioxide Added fossil CO₂ strengthens the greenhouse effect. CO · carbon monoxide Binds strongly to haemoglobin and interferes with the blood's oxygen transport. NOx · nitrogen oxides Can irritate airways, contribute to acidification and, with hydrocarbons and sunlight, form ground-level ozone. Traffic particles Exhaust and wear particles can enter and harm the respiratory system. Trafikverket: CO, NOx and particle mechanisms · Trafikverket: CO₂ and warming
questions.coverage_reasoning: Long-stored fossil carbon combines with oxygen, releases CO₂ and strengthens natural greenhouse effect.

questions.question_prompt: Where is the environmentally preferable place to wash a car?
questions.keyed_answer: A purpose-built wash facility that treats wastewater.
questions.teaching_excerpt: cannot be charged from an external electricity supply. Trafikverket: electric cars and hybrid types Choose a purpose-built automatic or self-service wash that collects and treats its wastewater. Washing on an ordinary street or driveway can carry oil, metals and cleaning chemicals into ground or surface water. Treatment reduces the problem but does not remove every pollutant. Follow the facility's product instructions and local water-protection rules. Göteborg environmental authority: washing and treatment Apply the comparison. A catalyst-equipped petrol car still releases fossil CO₂. An electric car avoids combustion exhaust on that drive, but needs a broader production-and-energy comparison. For either car, choose washing by how the dirty water is handled, rather than assuming a mild detergent makes street runoff harmless. Worked decision. Two vehicles are advertised using different environmental measures. One figure describes exhaust emissions under a test procedure; another describes noise. The learner does not rank them as though both figures measure the same thing. They first identify the question being answered and the information still missing.
questions.coverage_reasoning: Wastewater collection/treatment linked to oil, metals and chemicals; compatible products/local rules, no zero-pollution promise.

questions.question_prompt: Why can cities restrict studded tyres on particular roads?
questions.keyed_answer: Studs contribute to road wear and airborne particles.
questions.teaching_excerpt: f a proposed zone. Official local traffic regulations Studded tyres · A separate local restriction. Studs wear the road surface and create particles that can become airborne and enter the airways. Municipalities can restrict studded vehicles on particular roads or areas to address this problem. Check the current local decision in STFS, its dates, extent, exceptions and signs for your route. National permission to use studs in a season does not override a local prohibition. C44 denotes this restriction for motor vehicles other than moped class II; a supplementary panel can include that class too. Revisit the official C44 example in M07-L02. Trafikverket: stud-related particles · Transportstyrelsen: local restrictions, page 13 · Transportstyrelsen: C44
questions.coverage_reasoning: Stud wear → particles → airway harm; municipality can restrict road/area. Check STFS dates/extent/exceptions/signs, national season does not override local ban, correct C44 exception and cross-link M07-L02.
